subject: Energy
title: Coal and Urbanization
description: A short lesson to help you apply Coal and Urbanization.

hook.text: Coal powered the massive urban growth of the 1800s—factory cities like Manchester grew ten times in a century.

buildup.text: Mills and factories in coal-rich regions attracted millions—creating industrial cities with unprecedented populations.

discovery.text: Coal gas (from the 1810s) lit streets and homes—London was the first city with gas-lit streets, glowing through fog.

twist.text: Coal smoke poisoned those same cities—London's 'pea soup' fogs killed thousands, especially in the Great Smog of 1952.

climax.text: The 1956 Clean Air Act banned smoky fuels in London—transforming urban air quality and ending centuries of coal smog.

punchline.text: Coal built cities—then choked them with smoke.

quiz.question: What event prompted Britain's 1956 Clean Air Act?
